overview: Jumper wires are the connective tissue of every breadboard circuit, and they come in three end-type combinations that matter more than beginners initially expect: Male-to-Male (a solid pin on each end, for breadboard-to-breadboard connections), Male-to-Female (a pin on one end, a socket on the other, for connecting a breadboard to a header pin like an Arduino's), and Female-to-Female (a socket on both ends, for connecting two existing header pins together, e.g. two sensor breakout boards). Picking the wrong end-type is a common source of 'my circuit isn't working' confusion — a male end won't grip another male end at all.
simpleSummary: Small wires used to connect parts together on a breadboard.

specifications.wireGauge: Typically 22-26 AWG for hobby jumper wires
specifications.lengthOptions: Commonly sold in multiple lengths (10cm, 20cm, 30cm) in assorted color packs
specifications.currentRating: Light-duty — fine for logic signals and small sensor currents, not motor-level current

pinMap.name: Male End
pinMap.function: A solid metal pin, designed to insert into a breadboard hole or a female header socket.
pinMap.currentLimit: Light-duty, a few hundred mA typical for thin hobby wire
pinMap.gotcha: A male end cannot make a connection with another male end — check both ends of a wire before assuming a connection should work.

pinMap.name: Female End
pinMap.function: A socket/receptacle end, designed to slide over a male header pin (like those on an Arduino or a breakout board).
pinMap.gotcha: Female ends can sometimes make a loose or intermittent connection on worn pins — a wire that 'sometimes works' is often a female-end fit issue, not a code bug.

useCases.title: Breadboard circuit wiring
useCases.scenario: Connect components on a breadboard to each other and to a microcontroller.

useCases.title: Sensor breakout board connections
useCases.scenario: Connect two boards' header pins directly using F-F wires without a breadboard in between.

oftenConfusedWith: Solid-core hookup wire (for permanent soldered connections, not breadboard-friendly)
oftenUpgradedTo: Custom-length soldered wiring or a PCB for a finalized, permanent project
